– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,

Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test tries to check the behavior of ArrayUtils.addAll for arrays of different but related types, specifically `Integer[]` and `Long[]`, adding them together. The test expects an IllegalArgumentException for incompatible types.

The current implementation of ArrayUtils.addAll(T[] array1, T... array2) works as follows:
- It checks if either input array is null, and returns a clone of the other if so.
- It gets the component type of the first array (type1).
- It creates a new array of type1 with a size equal to the sum of the two arrays.
- It copies the elements of array1 into the new array.
- It then copies array2 into the new array using System.arraycopy.

The problem is that there is no explicit check for the compatibility of array2's runtime type elements with the component type of array1 before copying. System.arraycopy will throw ArrayStoreException if an element of array2 cannot be stored in the new array of type1, but this is a runtime exception that may not be clear.

The failed test expects ArrayUtils.addAll to detect this type incompatibility and throw an IllegalArgumentException instead, which is more informative and controlled.

The stack trace from the bug report also shows an ArrayStoreException at System.arraycopy call inside ArrayUtils.addAll, reinforcing that the code does not currently handle mismatched array types gracefully.

The root cause is that ArrayUtils.addAll does not check or validate element types in array2 against the component type of array1 before copying, leading to an ArrayStoreException that is not very clear. The method should catch or prevent this scenario and throw a better exception with a clearer message. This explains why the test fails and why the bug report complains about poor handling of mixed array types.

The recent bug reports are unrelated to this specific issue.

Summary:
- addAll uses System.arraycopy directly without type checks for array2.
- Type mismatch leads to ArrayStoreException.
- Test expects IllegalArgumentException instead for clarity.
- This issue is the root cause of the failure and error described.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
